original_target.title: Is maximality local for arbitrary plurisubharmonic functions?

full_original_statement:
Let $`\Omega\subset\mathbb C^n`$, $`n\ge2`$, be a domain and let $`u\in\mathrm{PSH}(\Omega)`$ satisfy $`u\not\equiv-\infty`$. Call $`u`$ **maximal** if, for every $`v\in\mathrm{PSH}(\Omega)`$ satisfying $`v\le u`$ outside a compact subset of $`\Omega`$, one has $`v\le u`$ throughout $`\Omega`$.

Suppose every point has an open neighborhood on which the restriction of $`u`$ is maximal. Must $`u`$ be maximal on $`\Omega`$? No boundedness, analytic-singularity or Monge–Ampère domain-of-definition assumption is imposed.

sources.scope_comparison: The actual local-to-global theorem requires locally analytic singularities c log|f|+O(1) with two-sided locally bounded remainder. Arbitrary singular psh functions in the target need not have this form or belong to Cegrell's domain of definition. The other October comparison paper has analytic/Cegrell restrictions; a smooth Hilbert-space theorem also does not apply. No full matching general claim found.
